Web Development: Angular is a TypeScript-based web framework. NgModule defines a compilation context for components, pipes, directives. @Component decorator defines a component. RxJS is used for reactive programming. The virtual DOM is a lightweight copy of the real DOM for efficient updates. REST stands for Representational State Transfer. POST creates resources, GET retrieves, PUT updates, DELETE removes. TypeScript is a typed superset of JavaScript. Components have templates, styles, and class logic.
Design: UX stands for User Experience. UI/UX design focuses on usability and aesthetics. Figma is widely used for prototyping and collaboration. Wireframes show layout and structure before visual design. 'Above the fold' means content visible without scrolling. Accessibility (a11y) ensures design is usable by people with disabilities. Design systems are collections of reusable components and standards. Prototyping helps validate ideas before development.
Marketing: SEO is Search Engine Optimization - improving visibility in search results. CTR is Click-Through Rate - ratio of clicks to impressions. A marketing funnel is the path from awareness to conversion. A/B testing compares two versions to find the better performer. KPIs are Key Performance Indicators for measuring success. Target audience, messaging, and channels are core marketing concepts.
Data Science: Overfitting occurs when a model performs well on training data but poorly on new data. EDA is Exploratory Data Analysis. A confusion matrix shows true vs predicted classifications. Cross-validation splits data to evaluate model performance without overfitting. Feature engineering transforms raw data for better model performance. Train/test split prevents data leakage during evaluation.
Mobile Development: React Native builds mobile apps using React and JavaScript. Flutter uses Dart and provides cross-platform apps. APK is Android Package Kit - the Android app format. Emulators simulate device hardware for testing. Native apps are built for a specific platform (iOS/Android). Hybrid apps use web technologies wrapped in a native container.
